narrative: Material PL1__MAFE6108 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.75) with a statistically significant upward trend (p=0.0017), and highly unstable lead times (CV=0.94). The current SAP safety stock of 0 units provides no buffer, making the 95% service level target unachievable. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 2,302 units and EOQ of 7,572 units is recommended to absorb demand and lead time variability while remaining within the 18,638-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The erratic demand regime (CV=0.75) with high non-zero fraction (90.8%) and unstable lead times warrants a continuous-review reorder-point model. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs at scale; the reorder point encodes both expected demand during lead time and a safety stock buffer calibrated to the 95th percentile of lead-time demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Transport lead time variability dominates 59.4% of total sigma_ltd variance. Any further deterioration in lead time consistency will increase safety stock requirements disproportionately. Current capacity headroom of 8,764 units is adequate.
